subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add browser private-network SSRF confirmation or allow/block policy, and which security/config shape should be supported first?
rationale: This changes browser egress security semantics, user approval UX, and public configuration behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the policy boundary.

options.title: Stage allow/block policy first
options.body: Approve a narrow first phase for explicit allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata blocking, then evaluate interactive confirmation after the core boundary is tested.

options.title: Approve confirmation UX now
options.body: Commit to interactive approval with timeout, rate-limit, redirect, DNS, and audit semantics across browser navigation paths before implementation starts.

options.title: Keep current strict/opt-in model
options.body: Reject the core expansion for now and keep strict default plus hostname exceptions and broad trusted-environment opt-in as the supported behavior.

recommendation.title: Stage allow/block policy first
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow first phase for explicit allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata blocking, then evaluate interactive confirmation after the core boundary is tested.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent browser config/docs/session history and are the best visible routing candidate for a browser security product decision.
